title: Boolean matrix multiplication

problem.name: Boolean matrix multiplication
problem.statement_latex: Given $A,B\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, output $C_{ij}=\bigvee_{k=1}^n(A_{ik}\wedge B_{kj})$. Let $\ell$ be the number of nonzero output entries. Complexity counts time with coherent indexed input access and explicit sparse output.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n\sqrt{\ell+1}+\ell\sqrt n)$ time by Le Gall. The Jeffery--Kothari--Magniez graph-collision algorithm uses $\widetilde\Theta(n\sqrt{\ell+1})$ queries, in the output-size range covered by its matching lower bound.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n\sqrt{\ell+1}+\ell\sqrt n)$ time by Le Gall. The Jeffery–Kothari–Magniez graph-collision algorithm uses $\widetilde\Theta(n\sqrt{\ell+1})$ queries, in the output-size range covered by its matching lower bound.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^2)$ input queries. For time, output-sparse matrix multiplication gives $\widetilde O(n^2)$ when $\ell\le n$ and $\widetilde O(n^{\omega(\delta-1,1,1)})$ when $\ell=n^\delta$ with $1\le\delta\le2$, by Abboud--Bringmann--Fischer--Kunnemann and Bennett--Gajulapalli--Golovnev--Warton. Here $\omega(a,b,c)$ is the rectangular matrix-multiplication exponent; the integer product has the same support as the Boolean product.
